cards.title: FPP chi=1/3 campaign, 2026-08-15 fire 4 - NOVELTY DOWNGRADE of the same day's transfer principle, restated self-contained so this row can be read alone. THE MATHEMATICS IS UNCHANGED: (C3) is constant-A doubling hence wall-equivalent, so the continuity route's content is transport only; and quantile interpolation between non-degenerate laws on [a,b] preserves non-degeneracy with modulus eta(h) <= h(b-a), so doubling for ONE such law would give Var = O(n^{1-log2/logM}) for EVERY such law. THE NOVELTY CLAIM IS DOWNGRADED to NEW IN THIS SPECIFIC FORM, NOT NEW IN KIND, on a literature pass run as a declared debt: (i) Chatterjee, 'The universal relation between scaling exponents in first-passage percolation', Annals of Math 177 (2013), arXiv 1105.4566, proves chi = 2 xi - 1 and states it is universal, independent of dimension AND of the law of the weights under moment assumptions - so distribution-independence of FPP exponents is an established theme; (ii) Damron-Hanson-Sosoe, arXiv 1306.1197 (PTRF), prove sublinear variance for GENERAL distributions directly (absolutely continuous, discrete, singular continuous, mixtures) under only 2 + log moments via a geometric average replacing BKS's randomised starting point - so the field gets distributional generality with NO transfer argument, under a moment condition strictly WEAKER than the bounded support the continuity lemma needs. The transfer principle is therefore narrower than the state of the art on the axis it trades in. It is not vacuous - the target transferred is the POLYNOMIAL n^{1-eps} that nobody has for any single law - but it must never be presented as a new idea about universality. chi = 1/3 UNMOVED.

cards.title: Burton-Keane Uniqueness of the Infinite Cluster
cards.body:
Let mu be a probability measure on {0,1}^{E(Z^d)} that is (i) invariant under the lattice translations, (ii) ERGODIC with respect to them, and (iii) has the FINITE ENERGY property: for every edge e, the conditional probability that e is open given the states of all other edges lies almost surely strictly between 0 and 1. Then the number of infinite open clusters is almost surely a constant taking the value 0 or 1. Each of the three hypotheses does work. Ergodicity is what makes the number a constant rather than a random variable; without it a mixture of two percolation measures is a counterexample. Finite energy is what rules out infinitely many infinite clusters, by allowing local modifications; a measure that deterministically forbids certain local patterns can have infinitely many. And the argument uses AMENABILITY of Z^d - on a regular tree or another nonamenable transitive graph there is genuinely a regime with infinitely many infinite clusters, so the theorem is false there. Bernoulli percolation satisfies all three hypotheses for every p, so its infinite cluster is unique whenever it exists. [Burton and Keane (1989), Comm. Math. Phys. 121; see Grimmett, Percolation, 2nd ed., Theorem 8.1]
translation invariance
ergodicity under the translations
finite energy
an amenable transitive graph such as Z^d; the theorem FAILS on nonamenable graphs

By translation invariance the expected number of trifurcations in a box of side 2n + 1 is delta (2n+1)^d. cards.title: Technique: Burton-Keane Uniqueness of the Infinite Cluster
cards.body:
TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For a translation-invariant, ergodic percolation measure on Z^d, or more generally on an amenable transitive graph, satisfying finite energy (insertion and deletion tolerance for each edge conditionally on the rest of the configuration), the number N of infinite open clusters is almost surely a constant in {0, 1, infinity}, and Burton and Keane's argument rules out 2 <= N < infinity as well as N = infinity: if there were at least two infinite clusters with positive density, a positive density of trifurcation points (local configurations forcing at least three disjoint infinite paths) would be forced, but a discrete isoperimetric counting argument on a large box shows the number of trifurcation points cannot exceed a quantity of the order of the box's boundary, contradicting positive density in the bulk unless N <= 1. It follows that N is almost surely 0 or 1. The argument does not apply to non-amenable graphs, where coexistence of infinitely many infinite clusters is a genuine, well-studied phenomenon rather than a proof artifact, and constancy of N itself (ruling out a mixture over the value of N) is a separate ergodic-theory step, not part of the trifurcation-counting argument. Typical failure: Applying Burton-Keane uniqueness to a non-amenable graph, such as a regular tree or a graph with exponential volume growth, and expecting a unique infinite cluster; the trifurcation-point isoperimetric argument fundamentally requires amenability, and on non-amenable graphs the coexistence of infinitely many infinite clusters, studied by Haggstrom, Peres and others, is a real phenomenon that this theorem simply does not rule out. Canonical reference: Burton and Keane, 1989, Communications in Mathematical Physics; Gandolfi, Keane and Newman, 1992, Probability Theory and Related Fields.
translation invariance, or more generally a transitive amenable group action, of the percolation measure
ergodicity of the measure under the translation group, needed to conclude N is almost surely constant
amenability of the underlying graph, i.e. subexponential boundary-to-volume ratio along a Folner sequence
finite energy or insertion and deletion tolerance for each edge's conditional state

cards.title: Open problem: No percolation at criticality on Z^d for 3 <= d <= 10
cards.body:
OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status no_resolution_found_in_documented_search; result status attempted_unsolved). Prove theta(p_c) = 0 for Bernoulli percolation on Z^d for every d >= 3; open for 3 <= d <= 10 (known for d >= 11 by Fitzner and van der Hofstad, and for d = 2). Source: Garban and Steif: Noise sensitivity of Boolean functions and percolation, lecture notes with open problems, Chapter XI Section 1, p. 136; also duminil_copin_icm_2018 Conjecture 1 p. 3 and duminil_copin_ising_potts_2017 Conjecture 1 p. 37. Status notes: Bounded search 2026-09-07: no resolution for 3 <= d <= 10 found; the d >= 11 result (Fitzner-van der Hofstad 2017) and the half-space result of Barsky-Grimmett-Newman remain the state of the art.

cards.title: Attempt on No infinite cluster at criticality on quasi-transitive graphs with p_c < 1
cards.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Split by growth type and identify the remaining cases precisely. Result: By Trofimov's theorem a quasi-transitive graph of polynomial growth is quasi-isometric to a Cayley graph of a virtually nilpotent group, and the critical behaviour of percolation is not a quasi-isometry invariant in general, so this does not reduce directly to Z^d; however the known proof for Z^2 (Harris-Kesten) and the high-dimensional proof (lace expansion, d >= 11) do not transfer either. Exponential growth is Hutchcroft's theorem. The remaining cases are (a) polynomial growth of degree 3 to 10 (and all virtually nilpotent non-abelian cases, e.g. the Heisenberg group of growth degree 4), where the problem is at least as hard as C0023, and (b) intermediate growth (Grigorchuk-type groups), where Hutchcroft's argument fails because it uses that the number of vertices at distance n grows exponentially to compare the cluster with a branching structure. For case (b) I checked the two known routes: the nonamenable route (Burton-Keane fails, so uniqueness monotonicity gives theta(p_c)=0 through the Benjamini-Lyons-Peres-Schramm argument) does not apply since intermediate-growth groups are amenable; the exponential-growth route uses a subadditivity argument on the expected number of vertices at distance n reached by the cluster, which requires growth rate > 1 in the exponential sense. Intermediate growth groups have growth exp(n^alpha), alpha < 1, which is superpolynomial, and Hutchcroft's argument actually needs only that the growth is faster than any polynomial? His proof uses the growth to show that the susceptibility is finite at p_c in a spherically-averaged sense via a comparison with a branching random walk with killing at rate given by the growth; I believe the argument requires exponential growth for the comparison to be uniform, so intermediate growth is a genuine gap. Recorded: the open cases are polynomial growth (degree 3 to 10 and non-abelian nilpotent) and intermediate growth. Obstruction: Polynomial growth is the Z^d problem; intermediate growth defeats the exponential-growth comparison.
